record.context_brief: Equivalence Principle as discriminator of gravity formulations
record.original_question: Can increasingly precise tests of the Equivalence Principle determine whether gravity should be formulated in a purely metric way or in a Palatini-type way with metric g and connection Γ treated as independent variables? More specifically, can Equivalence Principle measurements decide whether Γ is only the Levi-Civita connection of g or whether it may be a more general connection that is, in principle, disentangled from the metric?

evidence.quote: The Equivalence Principle (EP) is strictly related to the above considerations and could play a very relevant role in order to discriminate among theories.

In particular, it could specify the role of g and Γ selecting between the metric and Palatini formulation of gravity. In particular, precise measurements of EP could say us if Γ is only Levi - Civita or a more general connection disentangled, in principle, from g.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a spacetime described by a 4-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with a Lorentzian metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ and an affine connection $\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$. Two standard formulations of a gravitational theory are:

(i) the purely metric formulation, in which $\Gamma$ is postulated a priori to be the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, i.e. the unique torsion-free connection satisfying $\nabla_\lambda g_{\mu\nu}=0$, so that the metric is the only independent dynamical field; and

(ii) the Palatini (metric-affine) formulation, in which $g_{\mu\nu}$ and $\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ are treated as independent dynamical variables, with the relation between $\Gamma$ and $g$ (if any) determined by the field equations rather than imposed a priori.

The Equivalence Principle (EP), in its various formulations (weak, Einstein, strong), constrains the universality of free fall and the local validity of special-relativistic physics for test bodies. EP tests measure, for example, the Eötvös parameter $\eta=2|a_1-a_2|/|a_1+a_2|$ comparing the accelerations of bodies of differing composition in an external gravitational field.

Question: Can experimental tests of the Equivalence Principle, of arbitrarily increasing precision, in principle distinguish between the metric and Palatini formulations of gravity? More precisely, does there exist a class of EP-type observables whose outcomes determine whether the connection $\Gamma$ governing the motion of test bodies is necessarily the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, or whether $\Gamma$ may instead be a more general independent connection disentangled from $g$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g. a 2025 work on "Equivalent Gravities and the Equivalence Principle") continues to discuss how EP tests could in principle discriminate metric vs. Palatini/metric-affine formulations, and earlier results show that Palatini f(R) theories can induce EP violations. However, no consensus experimental or theoretical resolution has been reached, and current EP tests have not been shown to be sufficient on their own to discriminate the two formulations. The problem remains an active open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Equivalent Gravities and Equivalence Principle: Foundations and experimental implications
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses how EP tests can serve as discriminators among gravity formulations and considers the distinct dynamics of metric vs. connection.
status_evidence.claim: The discrimination between metric and Palatini-type formulations via EP tests is still an active research direction as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: Violation of the Equivalence Principle in Modified Theories of Gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Palatini f(R) gravity can induce gravitationally-mediated microscopic interactions leading to EP violations.
status_evidence.claim: Palatini formulations can in principle yield EP violations, suggesting EP measurements have discriminating power, though this has not been experimentally settled.

status_evidence.title: Precision Gravity Tests and the Einstein Equivalence Principle
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews precision EP tests and their relation to alternative gravity theories.
status_evidence.claim: Current precision EP tests have not conclusively distinguished metric from Palatini formulations.
